questions.q: What problem does dynamic provisioning solve compared to manually creating a PersistentVolume for every claim?
options: It avoids a human having to pre-create a real cloud disk through the Azure or AWS console before every PVC can bind
It removes the need for accessModes on a PVC entirely
It lets a PVC bind to a Pod directly without a PersistentVolume ever existing
It eliminates the need for a cluster to have any storage provisioner installed
questions.explain: Manually creating a PV for every claim doesn't scale once many applications need their own storage. Dynamic provisioning lets a provisioner create the disk automatically, triggered by the PVC itself.

questions.q: What does a StorageClass actually represent?
options: A piece of already-provisioned storage, the same as a PersistentVolume
A template naming a provisioner plugin and its parameters, used to create a disk on demand
A per-namespace quota limiting total PVC storage requests
A field inside a Pod spec that enables persistent storage
questions.explain: A StorageClass isn't storage itself — it's a recipe: it names which provisioner (CSI driver) to call and what parameters to pass it when a new disk needs to be created.

questions.q: In a StorageClass for AKS with `provisioner: disk.csi.azure.com`, what does that provisioner actually do when a matching PVC is created?
options: It formats the node's local disk and mounts it to the Pod
It is a CSI driver that calls the Azure API to create a real managed disk matching the StorageClass's parameters
It only validates YAML syntax and performs no real cloud action
It copies an existing Azure Disk's contents into a new PersistentVolume
questions.explain: disk.csi.azure.com is AKS's CSI driver for Azure Disk. When a PVC names a StorageClass using that provisioner, it actually calls the Azure API to create a managed disk and a matching PersistentVolume.

questions.q: What does `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer` change about when a disk gets created?
options: It prevents the disk from ever being deleted, regardless of reclaimPolicy
It creates the disk immediately when the StorageClass itself is created, before any PVC exists
It delays disk creation until a Pod using the claim is actually scheduled, so the disk lands in the right availability zone
It forces every PVC using that class to request exactly the same size
questions.explain: WaitForFirstConsumer delays provisioning until a Pod needing the volume is scheduled, so the disk is created in the same zone as that node instead of being provisioned somewhere unreachable.

questions.q: A PVC's manifest never sets `storageClassName`. Based on this lesson, what actually happens?
options: The PVC fails validation and is rejected by the API server
The PVC is permanently stuck Pending until a storageClassName is added
It is treated as requesting zero storage classes and never gets a disk
Kubernetes uses whichever StorageClass is marked as the cluster's default, if one exists
questions.explain: If storageClassName is omitted, Kubernetes falls back to the StorageClass carrying the is-default-class annotation — which is why kubectl get storageclass is worth checking before assuming what kind of disk a PVC will get.
